question: In the first phase of the Green Revolution (approximately mid 1960s upto mid 1970s), the use of HYV seeds was restricted to the more affluent states such as _________.

options.text: Punjab, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu

solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India began in the mid-1960s to address food security through the introduction of High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds.
 
• In its first phase, the use of HYV seeds was concentrated in states with favorable irrigation facilities and financial resources, such as Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• Punjab emerged as the epicenter of the Green Revolution due to its advanced irrigation systems and agricultural infrastructure.
 
• States like Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh also adopted HYV seeds, leveraging their fertile lands and irrigation networks.
 
• The success of the Green Revolution in these states significantly increased food grain production, contributing to India's self-sufficiency in food.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High Yielding Variety (HYV) Seeds:**

 
 
• HYV seeds are genetically modified to increase crop yield and are resistant to pests and diseases.
 
• The introduction of HYV seeds during the Green Revolution focused on crops like wheat, rice, and maize.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Green Revolution:**
 
 
• India transitioned from a food-deficient country to one of the largest producers of food grains globally.
 
• The revolution led to increased use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and improved irrigation techniques.
 
 
 
• **Challenges of the Green Revolution:**
 
 
• It caused environmental issues such as soil degradation and water depletion due to excessive use of fertilizers and irrigation.
 
• Regional disparities emerged as states with better resources benefited more than others.
 
 
 
• **Second Phase of Green Revolution:**
 
 
• The second phase focused on spreading the benefits to other regions, including Eastern India.
 
• Efforts were made to diversify crops and introduce sustainable farming practices.
